To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stabilizer for bipeding with toe support phase can be evaluated by two indicators, the floor reaction force and root mean square of CoM tracking error, and that the stabilizer can be tuned by the two policies, (1) and (2), to improve the walking performance.

(1) the proposed indicators are useful for the evaluation of stabilization, (2) the ZMP phase lead compensation should be applied to the sagittal motion only, and (3) the velocity dissipation should be reduced for reliable walking.

the stabilizer proposed by our previous work [10] is effective in stabilizing biped walking which mimics human gait and the quality of stabilization depends on the tuning of the control parameter, especially the ZMP phase lead compensation and ZMP control gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of a stabilizer of biped walk with the toe support phase.
the evaluation and tuning of a controller for a biped robot which has toe support.
the evaluation of a feedback controller for biped walking which is robust against model uncertainty and disturbances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the controller proposed here is not a good choice in terms of robustness.
our proposed stabilizer is not suitable for the control of a real humanoid robot.
the proposed controller can realize reliable biped walking with toe support phase, but that there are some room for improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stabilizer is effective to realize biped walk which has toe support, but the control parameter tuning should be done with consideration to velocity dissipation at toe support.
the ZMP control is effective to stabilize walking with toe support phase only when the velocity dissipation is sufficiently small.
the proposed stabilizer is effective in the sense that it is robust against the model uncertainty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stabilizer for toe support walking is different from the one for heel support walking.
the stabilizer for bipede walk with toe support can be designed by considering the dynamics of a linear inverted pendulum.
the stabilizer should not control the ZMP in a large region of toe support phase.
